question: Can a normalized high-frequency substitution between synchronized Klein sampler-latent trajectories preserve contours or portrait identity while leaving appearance free?
runtime_source: Exact Phase 4 cases, model, VAE, text encoder, resolution, CFG, Euler schedule, prompts, and seed policy

reference_analogue.initialization: Native Klein CONST source-img2img initialization with the same clean source, ordinary Gaussian endpoint, start sigma, and seed as target.
reference_analogue.conditioning: Empty conditioning at CFG 1.0, matching published FBSDiff reconstruction rather than inventing a source prompt.
reference_analogue.limitation: This is not DDIM inversion/reconstruction. It is the smallest deterministic stock-Klein analogue available under the fixed source-img2img contract.
reference_analogue.synchronization: Precompute reference accepted states at every target sigma; substitute reference state ordinal i into target state ordinal i before the target model evaluation.

band_policy.type: high-FBS for contour preservation and appearance divergence
band_policy.transform: orthonormal channel-wise 2D DCT over each [128,32,32] sampler latent
band_policy.mask: reference coefficients where (u+v)/31 > 5/63, equivalently integer u+v >= 3; target coefficients otherwise

calibration.rationale: Three of six evaluations is the nearest unswept integer span to published approximately 45-55% early calibration.

acceptance: The arm must qualitatively improve portrait identity, age, pose, and framing over Gaussian and FSS r=2 while retaining substantial bronze/material transformation. Scalar gains alone do not qualify.
tuning_policy: One normalized high band and one fixed calibration span. Do not tune after outputs.
